Background and objective: Long-term exposure to cadmium (Cd) causes renal dysfunction, but the change in renal function with exposure is unknown. We assessed the evolution of Cd-induced renal effects after a reduction in dietary exposure to Cd in rice. Methods: Four hundred twelve residents in previously Cd-polluted and nonpolluted areas were examined twice, in 1998 and in 2006. Changes in blood Cd, urinary Cd, and kidney function [ N -acetyl-β- d -glucosaminidase (NAG), β 2 -microglobulin, and albumin in urine] were measured. Results: In the most polluted area, mean blood Cd was 8.9 μg/L and 3.3 μg/L in 1998 and in 2006, respectively, and urinary Cd was 11.6 and 9.0 μg/g creatinine. Urinary albumin in 1998 increased with urinary Cd, but no such exposure–response relation appeared for 2006 albumin versus urinary Cd 1998, indicating recovery. Other biomarkers of kidney function were also elevated in 1998. Partial recovery was observed for NAG among women and was suggested for β 2 -microglobulin among young individuals. The probability of having β 2 -microglobulin levels above the 95th percentile in 2006 was high in those with elevated β 2 -microglobulin in 1998 [odds ratio (OR) = 24.8; 95% confidence interval (CI): 11.2, 55.3] compared with albumin (OR = 3.0; 95% CI: 1.2, 7.5) and NAG (OR = 2.6; 95% CI: 1.6, 4.4). Conclusions: Results suggest that a Cd-mediated increase in urinary albumin excretion is reversible upon substantial reduction of exposure. For markers of tubular effects, we observed a tendency toward improvement but not complete recovery. Data from repeated observations suggest that β 2 -microglobulin may be more informative than NAG as an indicator for an individual’s future tubular function. albumin β 2 -microglobulin cadmium environmental exposure N -acetyl-β- d -glucosaminidase renal function Cadmium (Cd) has a very long biological half-life in humans (10–30 years). Occupational or environmental exposure to Cd can cause different health effects, one of the most prominent being kidney damage as a result of Cd accumulation in the kidney ( Nordberg et al. 1971 , 2007 ). The evolution of Cd-related renal effects after changes in exposure conditions (i.e., cessation of or reduction in Cd exposure) is now being discussed in the scientific literature. An issue of major concern is whether renal effects of Cd are permanent, or whether renal function may recover after exposure ceases. Some authors have observed that severe renal tubular damage is irreversible in workers [urinary Cd (UCd) > 20 μg/g creatinine] previously exposed to high levels of Cd in the workplace ( Jarup et al. 1993 ; Roels et al. 1997 ). Iwata et al. (1993) reported that renal dysfunction in individuals environmentally exposed to Cd via food became worse over time, even though exposure decreased from > 200 μg/day to half that value 14 years later, with a corresponding reduction in UCd from 8.5 to 6 μg/g creatinine. Hotz et al. (1999) , on the other hand, reported that mild and early forms of renal dysfunction improved in a population that had been environmentally exposed to Cd: mean UCd excretion and blood Cd (BCd) at baseline were 8.9 nmol/24 hr and 9.4 nmol/L (~ 1 μg/L), respectively, for men, and 8.8 nmol/24 hr and 10.9 nmol/L for women. We previously published data from a 3-year follow-up (1995–1998) of 148 individuals who stopped consuming rice with high Cd content, including biomarkers of kidney function at baseline and after exposure ceased ( Wu et al. 2008 ). The geometric mean (GM) of UCd among these individuals was 3.7 μg/g creatinine at baseline and 5.5 μg/g creatinine 3 years later ( p = 0.064). The results indicated that the Cd-induced renal dysfunction might be reversible if baseline exposure is relatively low (UCd < 10 μg/g creatinine) before exposure decrease but may be irreversible or increased among those with higher exposure at baseline. Here, we present data from 1998 and 2006 on 412 individuals from the same population as in the previous 3-year follow-up ( Wu et al. 2008 ). Our aim was to evaluate changes in the prevalence of impaired kidney function after cessation of exposure to contaminated rice in relation to the initial exposure level and other characteristics such as age and sex. We measured three different biomarkers of kidney function [urinary N -acetyl-β- d -glucosaminidase (NAG), β 2 -microglobulin, and albumin] and also evaluated the ability of each biomarker to predict future impairment in the same individual. The present study was part of a larger prospective study that also evaluated bone effects after reduction in Cd exposure ( Chen et al. 2009a , 2009b ).

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigates the long-term evolution of cadmium (Cd)-induced renal effects over an 8-year period (1998-2006) in residents from previously Cd-polluted areas of Zhejiang Province, China, following a substantial reduction in dietary Cd exposure. It assessed changes in kidney function biomarkers to determine the reversibility of Cd-induced renal damage. Key findings include the reversibility of Cd-mediated increases in urinary albumin excretion, while renal tubular damage markers (NAG,  2-microglobulin) showed only partial recovery, with  2-microglobulin being a more robust predictor of future tubular function.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Reduction in environmental and dietary cadmium exposure
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The study tracked 412 residents for 8 years (1998-2006) following a substantial reduction in chronic cadmium exposure (originally from contaminated rice and water for ~30 years). In highly polluted areas, mean blood Cd decreased from 8.9  5g/L to 3.3  5g/L, and urinary Cd from 11.6  5g/g creatinine to 9.0  5g/g creatinine. Baseline exposure was significantly elevated (UCd ~10x, BCd ~2-3x reference levels, with BCd in highly polluted areas up to 14  5g/L). Blood Cd showed a more pronounced decrease than urinary Cd, reflecting recent versus long-term exposure reduction. No explicit dose-response comparisons for the reduction itself were reported, but reversibility of renal dysfunction was suggested for individuals with baseline urinary Cd < 10  5g/g creatinine.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Elevated at baseline, with partial and incomplete recovery observed, particularly among women, while overall levels increased in some groups.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher at baseline in highly polluted areas (p < 0.001), exceeding age-adjusted cut points (9.8 U/g creatinine in 1998, 16.6 U/g creatinine in 2006). Levels increased overall in some individuals (p < 0.01 in 2006). Partial recovery was observed, primarily among women, while for men, levels tended to be higher in 2006. Recovery was incomplete; the decrease in prevalence of elevated NAG (UCd > 20  5g/g creatinine group) was not statistically significant (p = 0.06). Baseline NAG was a weak predictor for future elevation (OR = 2.6).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A lysosomal enzyme abundantly present in renal proximal tubular cells; increased urinary excretion indicates tubular membrane damage or dysfunction.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Chronic environmental cadmium exposure and its reduction over an 8-year period (1998-2006) in a human population.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates renal tubular damage and impaired kidney function. While an early sign of tubular membrane damage, it is less informative than  2-microglobulin for predicting future tubular function. Incomplete recovery suggests ongoing or residual impairment, with potential sex-specific responses.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significantly elevated at baseline, showing a tendency toward improvement or slight recovery in some groups (e.g., young individuals), but with a high probability of sustained elevation.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher at baseline in highly polluted areas (p < 0.001), exceeding age-adjusted cut points (0.890 mg/g creatinine in 1998, 1.028 mg/g creatinine in 2006). Levels increased overall in some individuals (p < 0.01 in 2006). While some slight recovery was suggested (especially in young individuals), there was little evidence of complete recovery. Elevated  2-microglobulin in 1998 was a strong predictor for elevated levels in 2006 (OR = 24.8; 95% CI: 11.2, 55.3), significantly higher than for albumin (OR = 3.0) and NAG (OR = 2.6). Individuals with baseline urinary  2-microglobulin > 300  5g/g creatinine experienced a greater decline in eGFR after 5 years.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A small protein normally filtered by glomeruli and almost completely reabsorbed by renal proximal tubules; its excessive presence in urine indicates renal tubular reabsorption dysfunction or damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Chronic environmental cadmium exposure and its reduction over an 8-year period (1998-2006) in a human population.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates renal tubular damage and impaired kidney function. It is a strong prognostic factor and a robust predictor of persistent and future tubular dysfunction, being more informative than NAG.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Initially increased significantly with cadmium exposure, but showed clear and significant recovery/reversibility after reduction in exposure.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly higher at baseline in highly polluted areas (p < 0.001), increasing with urinary Cd in 1998, and exceeding age-adjusted cut points (14.6 mg/g creatinine in 1998, 21.7 mg/g creatinine in 2006). Post-reduction, mean levels in 2006 significantly decreased from baseline (p < 0.01) in highly polluted areas for both sexes. A clear recovery was observed, independent of UCd value, with no exposure-response relation in 2006 compared to 1998, and a significant decline in prevalence of elevated albumin (p < 0.05 for UCd > 5  5g/g creatinine groups).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A major plasma protein whose excessive excretion in urine (albuminuria) signifies compromised glomerular filtration barrier integrity and glomerular damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Chronic environmental cadmium exposure and its reduction over an 8-year period (1998-2006) in a human population.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates glomerular dysfunction and damage. The Cd-mediated increase in urinary albumin excretion is a reversible effect, suggesting temporary damage that resolves after substantial reduction in exposure.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significantly higher at baseline, then substantially decreased after reduction in exposure.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Baseline geometric mean blood Cd was 2–3 times higher than nonpolluted reference values, with levels up to 14  5g/L (IQR 5–14  5g/L) and most residents in highly polluted areas > 5  5g/L in 1998. Following exposure reduction, mean blood Cd in the most polluted area decreased from 8.9  5g/L (1998) to 3.3  5g/L (2006). This decrease was observed across all surveyed individuals, was more pronounced in polluted areas, and responded more significantly to exposure reduction than urinary Cd.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Primarily indicates recent or ongoing cadmium exposure and reflects the current body burden of the metal, responding more quickly to exposure changes.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Chronic environmental cadmium exposure from contaminated rice and water, and subsequent reduction in exposure over an 8-year period.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Serves as a key determinant of Cd exposure, reflecting recent changes and overall body burden. A decrease confirms substantial reduction in exposure and may contribute to renal recovery, particularly for albuminuria. It is associated with renal damage, hypertension, and decreased GFR.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Significantly higher at baseline, showing a limited but statistically significant decrease after exposure reduction, predominantly in the most polluted areas.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Baseline geometric mean urinary Cd was approximately 10 times higher than nonpolluted reference values, with most residents in highly polluted areas > 5  5g/g creatinine in 1998. In the most polluted area, urinary Cd decreased from 11.6  5g/g creatinine (1998) to 9.0  5g/g creatinine (2006). A previous 3-year follow-up showed a slight increase in GM UCd from 3.7 to 5.5  5g/g creatinine (p=0.064) in a subset. A limited but statistically significant decrease was observed in the highly exposed area. Individuals with the highest UCd in 1998 (> 20  5g/g creatinine) experienced decreased eGFR in 2006.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects cumulative long-term cadmium exposure and the accumulated body burden, primarily stored in the kidneys.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Chronic environmental cadmium exposure from contaminated rice and water, and subsequent reduction in exposure over an 8-year period.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A key determinant of chronic Cd exposure and total body burden, associated with renal dysfunction and kidney damage. Higher levels predict decreased eGFR, and reversibility of renal dysfunction is linked to lower baseline UCd levels (< 10  5g/g creatinine).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Excessive excretion reported due to chronic exposure.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A small protein normally reabsorbed by the renal tubules; its excessive excretion indicates renal tubular dysfunction.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Chronic environmental cadmium exposure causing renal damage.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Determined by Jaffe reaction method and used to standardize urine spot samples, ensuring all urinary parameters were adjusted for dilution.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A waste product of muscle metabolism, excreted at a relatively constant rate; commonly used to adjust for urine dilution in spot samples.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Used for standardizing urinary biomarker measurements in environmental cadmium exposure studies.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Essential for accurate assessment of other urinary kidney function markers by accounting for urine dilution variability.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: In 2006, serum creatinine concentration was significantly higher in the highly polluted area compared to other areas (p < 0.01). Serum creatinine data was only available for 2006.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A waste product of muscle metabolism, used as an indicator of kidney function; elevated levels suggest impaired renal clearance.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-cessation of cadmium exposure (8-year follow-up) for assessing overall renal function.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates kidney function; higher levels suggest potential kidney impairment, especially in highly polluted areas, serving as a crucial indicator for diagnosing chronic kidney disease.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Declined, specifically in individuals with the highest baseline urinary cadmium.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Estimated using the Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration equation (in mL/min/1.73 m2). While no overall differences were noted between nonpolluted and polluted areas in 2006, eGFR significantly decreased only in individuals with the highest urinary Cd in 1998 (> 20  5g/g creatinine) compared to those with < 2  5g/g creatinine UCd. Individuals with baseline urinary  2-microglobulin > 300  5g/g creatinine also experienced a greater decline in eGFR after 5 years, although renal filtration in polluted areas was comparable to controls by 2006 for some.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Measures the rate at which kidneys filter blood, providing an overall assessment of kidney excretory and filtration function.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Assessment of renal function after chronic cadmium exposure and subsequent reduction, particularly in polluted areas and in individuals with high past urinary cadmium.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A crucial indicator for diagnosing and staging chronic kidney disease; lower values suggest kidney impairment. A significant decrease, even if localized to those with historical high exposure, indicates persistent kidney impairment.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased urinary metallothioneins were observed after cessation of oral cadmium exposure in an animal study.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A family of 6- to 7-kDa stress proteins, rich in cysteine and divalent metals, involved in metal homeostasis and detoxification.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Cessation of oral cadmium exposure (demonstrated in an animal study).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Potentially an informative marker to evaluate recovery of cadmium-mediated renal tubular dysfunction after exposure reduction.
